title: Lancashire Hotpot
subtitle: Northern English lamb and onion stew with a sliced potato crust
excerpt: Lancashire hotpot is the great dish of the industrial north of England: lamb chops and onions layered with stock under a thick crust of overlapping sliced potatoes, baked until the meat is tender and the potatoes are golden on top and soft underneath. It is one of the most satisfying cold-weather dishes in British cooking.
sourceNotes: Lancashire hotpot is the defining dish of Lancashire and the industrial towns of northern England. It was the working-class meal of the 19th century cotton mill towns -- cheap cuts of lamb and potatoes that could be left in the oven all day while the household worked. The sliced potato lid is distinctive: it seals in the steam, cooking the meat below while forming a golden crust on top.

recipe.temperatureNote: Increase to 200C for the final 20 minutes to brown the potato crust

content.text: The lamb chops go in raw -- no browning. The long, slow cook in the oven does all the work. The potatoes should be sliced thinly and evenly (about 3 to 4 mm) and arranged overlapping so they form a solid crust. Brush them generously with butter before and again halfway through to get the best colour.

items.prepNote: middle neck chops or shoulder chops

content.text: Preheat the oven to 160C. Season {{lamb-chops}} lamb chops with {{salt-table}} salt and {{black-pepper}} pepper. Layer them in a deep ovenproof dish with {{onion}} onion, {{carrots}} carrots, {{thyme-fresh}} thyme, and {{bay-leaves}} bay leaves between the layers. Pour {{lamb-stock}} stock over.

Arrange {{potatoes-floury}} sliced potatoes on top in overlapping layers, completely covering the meat. Season with {{salt-table}} salt and brush generously with {{unsalted-butter}} melted butter. Cover with foil or a lid.

Bake for 2 hours. Remove the foil, brush the potatoes again with {{unsalted-butter}} butter, and increase the oven to 200C. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the potato crust is golden and crisp. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The potato crust is pale and soft
items.cause: Not enough butter, or the oven was not increased in temperature at the end.
items.fix: Brush with more melted butter and put under the grill for 5 minutes to brown. The potato crust needs both heat from above and fat to colour properly.

content.text: Lancashire hotpot is inseparable from the industrial north of England. It is the dish of Bolton, Preston, Blackburn, and the mill towns of the 19th century. It is still widely eaten across Lancashire and Greater Manchester as a pub meal and a home staple. The Coronation Street version -- the hotpot made by Betty Williams in the fictional Rovers Return pub -- made it famous across Britain.
